# 📢 NH Reader v0.7.3 — Manual Signed Builds & Restored iOS Support

**Release Date:** 2026-10-01  
**Tag:** [`v0.7.3`](https://github.com/HELIX-Origin/NH-Reader/releases/tag/v0.7.3)

NH Reader v0.7.3 changes how the project distributes application packages. Because we cannot reliably provide properly signed release binaries, automated packaging and release-asset publishing have been removed. This source release has no prebuilt application downloads, and we will not publish unsigned assets. Anyone producing a distributable build must compile it locally and sign it with credentials they control.

---

## 🌟 What's New in v0.7.3

### 📦 Manual Builds and Platform Signing

- **No automated package publishing** — GitHub Actions no longer builds or uploads application installers, archives, or mobile packages. The release contains source only; no release assets are available to download.
- **Local signing commands** — `package.json` now includes signing commands for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and iOS. Signing keys, certificates, and provisioning profiles remain under the builder's control and must never be committed.
- **Platform builds** — Build desktop packages with `npm run build:app`; initialize/build Android with `npm run mobile:android:init` and `npm run mobile:android:build`; initialize/build iOS with `npm run mobile:ios:init` and `npm run mobile:ios:build`.

### 🍎 iOS Support Clarified

iOS support was restored previously, but several project pages continued to say that iOS was unsupported. This release corrects those statements: Tauri iOS builds are supported on macOS with Xcode and valid Apple signing credentials. They remain community-supported and untested by the maintainer.

---

## 🛠️ Build and Sign Locally

There are no prebuilt release assets. Build on the target platform and use your own signing credentials:

- **Windows:** `npm run build:app`, then `npm run sign:windows`. Place your PFX at `certificates/nh-reader-codesign.pfx`; the script can generate a local self-signed certificate if none exists, but self-signed certificates are not trusted publisher identities.
- **macOS:** `npm run build:app`, then `npm run sign:macos -- "<Developer ID Application identity>" "src-tauri/target/release/bundle/macos/NH Reader.app"`. Notarization is a separate Apple distribution step.
- **Linux:** `npm run build:app`, then `npm run sign:linux -- path/to/package`; verify with `gpg --verify path/to/package.asc path/to/package`.
- **Android:** `npm run mobile:android:init`, `npm run mobile:android:build`, then `npm run sign:android -- path/to/release.keystore --ks-key-alias <alias> path/to/app.apk`.
- **iOS:** On macOS with Xcode and a valid Apple signing identity/provisioning profile, run `npm run mobile:ios:init`, then `npm run sign:ios -- CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=<team-id> CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="Apple Distribution" PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER=<profile-name>`.

Do not commit private keys, keystores, certificates, or provisioning profiles. Never distribute an unsigned package as a release asset.
